about.heroSubtitle: Discover our mission, history, and impact on election observation in Africa.
about.dimensionsContext: The eight dimensions used in this assessment are anchored in established international norms and best practices for election observation, including the African Charter on Democracy, Elections, and Governance (AU, 2007) and the Declaration of Principles for International Election Observation (2005). They reflect a holistic understanding that credible citizen election observation extends far beyond the events of election day — the ability of observers to contribute meaningfully to electoral integrity is deeply influenced by the political climate, legal frameworks, institutional arrangements, and the overall state of civic space in which they operate.
about.dimensionsIntro: Our monitoring framework focuses on eight key dimensions that define civic space for election observers:
about.methodologyIntro: AfEONet uses a rigorous methodology to assess the state of civic space for election observers. Our approach combines qualitative and quantitative data collection to provide a comprehensive picture of the situation.
about.colorCodingIntro: We use a color coding system to visually represent the different civic space situations:
about.dataCollectionText: Our data collection process involves a network of focal persons in different African countries. These individuals are trained to observe and document the state of civic space according to our eight dimensions. The collected data is then validated by our team of administrators before being published on the platform.
about.scoresDocumentNote: Full country-by-country scores and supporting evidence are documented in the source report: "AfEONet Report 2025 — Eyes on the Ballot Watchers." A downloadable copy will be linked here once published.
about.joinNetworkText: Are you an election observer, civil society organization, or simply interested in our work? Join our network to contribute to monitoring civic space in Africa.
